A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BTimer work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across reflow and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original BTimer reconstruction results on dynamic and static benchmarks, including Tables 1–3 and S2–S3, together with qualitative evaluations and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds quantitative component ablations, batch-size training curves, and resource measurements in the appendix.

M1.justification: The BTimer architecture, timestamp embeddings, Gaussian prediction, supervision losses, inference procedure, NTE module and three-stage training curriculum are retained. Expanded contribution summaries do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The training datasets in Table S1 and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including DyCheck, NVIDIA Dynamic Scene, DAVIS, RE10K and Tanks & Temples. The new analyses vary settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: New Figure S3 compares BTimer's computation cost with LVSM, LRM, T-NeRF, HyperNeRF and Nerfies, introducing LVSM and LRM into a reported cost comparison. Comparator membership in the retained reconstruction benchmarks is unchanged; Depth Warp remains in Tables 1–2 despite its removed prose mention.

E3.justification: Table S2 identifies the previously two-view-described best static result as using four views and adds a separate two-view result. Reported training resources change from 64 to 32 A100 GPUs, without establishing reruns. New protocols include 1/8/32-GPU batch-size comparisons and four-context-frame quantitative ablations. The largest timing case changes from 512×896 to 512×512.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the analyses beyond v1's qualitative component ablations: Table S4 quantifies the effects of static pretraining, dataset diversity, static co-training and interpolation supervision. Figure S4 adds batch-size sensitivity across training stages, while Figure S3 analyzes computation cost as the number of reconstructed scenes grows.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments. The new batch-size curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table S2 adds two-view Ours-Static results of 26.49 PSNR, 0.886 SSIM and 0.096 LPIPS; 28.91/0.920/0.070 is retained with a four-view qualifier. Table S4 adds ablation PSNRs ranging from 17.94 to 24.00. New cost, training-loss and memory results accompany revised timing coverage, while the standalone NTE timing is removed. Existing main benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical input definitions, Gaussian parameterization and unprojection, time-embedding construction and loss equation are unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: The core claims about feed-forward dynamic reconstruction, the bullet-time formulation, static/dynamic generalization, efficient inference and NTE's handling of fast motion are retained. The expanded introduction consolidates contributions already stated in v1, and the conclusion retains its scientific claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix B interprets training cost as amortized across scenes and argues that larger batches benefit training. v2 removes the DAVIS passage asserting that recovered depth demonstrates correct geometry enabled by widely separated input views. The explicit geometry-accuracy and view-extrapolation limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 revises the reported training hardware to 32 A100 GPUs, specifies the inference GPU and DyCheck's 360×480 evaluation resolution, and adds memory measurements and batch-related details. It newly promises source code and pretrained checkpoints, without establishing their release. The separate NTE runtime disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained, but v2 refines the introduction's positioning of static feed-forward methods and explicitly relates training choices and amortized computation to LVSM, LRM and GS-LRM. These are limited positioning changes rather than an expanded literature review.

P1.justification: Selected introduction, contribution-summary and experimental paragraphs are rewritten, and 'Timing' becomes 'Inference Cost.' A new Appendix B shifts the existing supplementary sections B/C to C/D. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures S3–S4 and Tables S4–S5, expands Table S2 with a row and input-view footnote, and relocates existing displays including Figures 4 and 7 and Table S2. The document template and existing qualitative image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The quantitative ablations and batch-size, computation and memory analyses strengthen support for the training choices and improve resource transparency. Table S2 also clarifies the distinction between two-view and four-view static results. The gain is limited because Table 3(a) still presents the earlier 0.070 LPIPS without the four-view qualifier, and the appendix's two-view/best-model prose is not fully reconciled with the revised table.
